records.material_pending_reason: The independently produced wetland inventory separates Cauchari and Olaroz into two salar nuclei and describes the intervening Archibarca fan as a barrier. Imagery shows the narrow, modified inter-salar setting, but neither it nor the inspected prose establishes the selected passage through that setting. This is a specific transfer gap, not a demand for a river line across an otherwise continuous single playa.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The Tocomar–Campo Amarillo approach toward the southeastern Cauchari receiving area. The name is not extended to every short headward feeder, the long Cauchari salt-floor continuation, the inter-salar passage or the Olaroz terminal.
records.completion_scope: The selected southern approach corresponds to the Tocomar–Campo Amarillo valley and southeastern Cauchari entry. Its long northward continuation occupies the Cauchari saline depression before reaching the southern Olaroz salt floor. The intervening passage around the Archibarca alluvial-fan and road/evaporation-pond setting remains unsupported as a selected through-connection. The actual terminal is geographically accounted for within Olaroz; that does not close the intervening gap.
records.supported_name_scope: The Tocomar–Campo Amarillo approach toward the southeastern Cauchari receiving area. The name is not extended to every short headward feeder, the long Cauchari salt-floor continuation, the inter-salar passage or the Olaroz terminal.

scope_limits: Río Tocomar is a bounded upper-corridor identification; the exact short headward opening is not independently named.
The geographic terminal in Olaroz does not establish passage from Cauchari across the intervening fan/road/pond setting.
Imagery dates, current water presence, hydraulic direction and infrastructure operation are unverified. No interpretation of mine operations or precise engineering connections is made.

The inventory is an ecological mapping project. Its derived hydrology is not an independent survey of every channel, and its barrier statement cites García. The original García publication was not acquired or treated as directly read.
The territorial-plan annex is a compilation. Only the specifically identified Puna2014 constituent and bounded prose are used; other compiled documents and map panels are not evidence.
No discovery snippet, stopped original, unseen figure or uninspected companion is used as substantive evidence.

records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative receiving-system identity across the selected western lake branch, distinct Grand Lake Stream, West Branch St. Croix lake corridor, Grand Falls and Woodland impoundments and lower St. Croix estuary. records.completion_scope: Five newly acquired USGSTopo originals establish the selected opening, Pleasant–Scraggly–Junior–West Grand lake chain, Grand Lake Stream, Big–Long–Lewey/Princeton corridor, Grand Falls connection and lower St. Croix receiving corridor through the actual estuarine ending. Independent IJC study and Waterway Commission prose corroborate the named branch and impoundment connections. St. Croix River is supported as a representative system identity; no scalar or accepted name is applied.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative receiving-system identity across the selected western lake branch, distinct Grand Lake Stream, West Branch St. Croix lake corridor, Grand Falls and Woodland impoundments and lower St. Croix estuary. It does not rename the unnamed opening, any lake or the distinct stream as one scalar river.

scope_limits: The chosen northwestern feeder has no supported separate name in the sources read; its name remains null.
St. Croix River is a representative receiving-system identity, not a single natural-river label extending over every upstream lake and distinct Grand Lake Stream reach.

The lower selected fragments are generalized. The evidence establishes the connected receiving corridor and actual estuarine setting, without assigning exact channel banks, dam-versus-powerhouse routes, or hydronym-transition positions.
The final receiving embayment is connected to the mapped St. Croix estuary; the selected route does not require or establish a farther route to the full Passamaquoddy Bay mouth.
The fish-passage study cover date is 2021 while running headers print 2020 and the filename contains 2019. Cover, title, authors and contract identifiers establish the exact document used.
No official naming register or present operating condition was verified.

records.completion_scope: Kirchoffer River is supported as the representative identity of the selected Southampton Island river system. Three photographic originals establish the chosen opening, all18 parts and intervening joins, lower widenings, gorge and actual South Bay terminal. Bird1953’s own regional maps and field prose provide the name and coastal identity. Official registry status and a whole-feature scalar name remain unverified.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative identity for the connected selected river system, supported by an independently authored named regional field-study map and full ordinary photographic corridor correspondence. The northern feeder and river widenings are included as components without imposing the same scalar name on every local reach or waterbody.

scope_limits: The river name is supported at representative system scope by the historical primary field publication; current formal registry status is unverified.
The named publication’s regional cartography is generalized. Photographic correspondence supplies the detailed route, without inventing a name for each feeder or river widening.

Cloud patches and seasonal snow reduce individual-pixel detail in the upper imagery, but the entering and leaving channel, valley form and joins establish the same ordinary corridor; no exact current wetted-thread claim is made.

Optional held sources and the absent pocket map were not needed for the established ordinary geographic correspondence. Their restrictions and content limitations remain separate from the single completed primary status.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
